rules.summary: IDs are unique in their declared scope and globally where the contract says globally unique.
State definitions are unique, cannot overlap a JSON-object root, and every expression/action path resolves to one definition.
No two selectors in one node may match the same event, including wildcard source or qualifier overlap.
Fallback routes are last; at most one navigation action exists and it is the final action.
References resolve, finite experiences can reach an ending, and all graph nodes are reachable from entry.
Renderer, gesture, spatial, audio, and extension features declare every required host capability.
Anchors remain in bounds, reference the same scene, and keyframes preserve resolved geometry kind and polygon topology for every orientation.
Gesture references resolve and a press-hold duration fits within its active window.
Telemetry payload fields are declared, type-compatible, complete, and never read sensitive state.
The publisher fully materializes and validates Runtime Manifest v2 before Java stores its opaque JSON value.
All events share session, game, manifest, build, and content-version identities.
Event IDs and sequence numbers are unique and sequences are strictly increasing.
clientWriteId is idempotent and Java atomically compares both session and player-state versions.
